To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a signal conditioning unit for aeroengine rotating sensors, capable of operating at 235 $^o$C and generating a pulse signal with high linearity and high dynamic range, was developed and tested.
we have developed and fabricated an integrated signal conditioning circuit for aeroengine rotating sensors that can operate at high temperatures and has a wide dynamic range.
a mixed signal unit capable of sensing signals up to 235 Celsius was successfully developed and tested on a rotating engine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a high temperature sensor interface circuit for the aeroengine.
the development of a high temperature mixed signal integrated circuit (IC) for the measurement of peak values of high frequency signals in rotating systems.

the development and testing, in a high temperature environment, of an electronic unit that is capable of sensing wide range signals and generating an analog output proportional to the peak of the applied input signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mixed signal unit has been successfully developed and tested for aeroengine applications.

a mixed signal unit capable of sensing and converting wide dynamic range signals into digital format has been developed and tested for the first time in an SOI CMOS technology for an aeroengine application.
the mixed signal unit is an excellent solution for the high temperature signal conditioning requirements for aeroengines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a signal conditioning unit for aeronautical rotating systems that can be utilized in a wide range of temperatures and is capable of sensing wide range signals with a very high linearity and resolution.
we developed a high temperature signal conditioner for aeroengine sensors and the unit was shown to operate up to 235$^\circ$ Celsius.
the developed unit is the first integrated mixed signal unit for aeroengine applications that is capable of operating at high temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a fully integrated high temperature signal conditioning system can be designed and fabricated in a commercial foundry and can be used in the harsh environment of an aeroengine.
the high temperature signal conditioning circuit can be implemented on a mixed signal SOI CMOS chip.
it is feasible to develop a signal conditioning unit for a rotating aeroengine on silicon-on-insulator CMOS technology.
